definitions.gloss: step; difference in level; uneven surface
definitions.explanation: A difference in height between two surfaces, such as a step at a doorway, a curb, or an uneven pavement. Often mentioned as a hazard or accessibility concern.

examples.japanese: ⟦{足元|あしもと}→足元：04096_ashimoto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{段差|だんさ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}をつけて⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please watch out for the step.

examples.japanese: {段差|だんさ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦つまずいて→つまずく：06970_tsumazuku⟧⟦{転|ころ}んで→転ぶ：00863_korobu⟧しまった。
examples.english: I tripped on a step and fell.

examples.japanese: ⟦バリアフリー→バリアフリー：11153_bariafurii⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{段差|だんさ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧なくして、⟦{車椅子|くるまいす}→車椅子：10533_kurumaisu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{移動|いどう}→移動：01741_idou⟧しやすく⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Barrier-free buildings eliminate steps so that wheelchair users can move around easily.

notes:
A very practical everyday word. You will see {段差|だんさ}⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧ (watch your step) signs in many buildings and public spaces in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {段差|だんさ}⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧ (watch your step — sign)
- {段差|だんさ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧なくす (to eliminate steps / make step-free)
- {段差|だんさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ (step-free, level)
- {段差|だんさ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦つまずく→つまずく：06970_tsumazuku⟧ (to trip on a step)

Important in discussions of ⟦バリアフリー→バリアフリー：11153_bariafurii⟧ (barrier-free design) and accessibility. Small {段差|だんさ} at entrances and between rooms are common in older Japanese buildings.
